title: Why traditional security checks are failing in the age of AI-driven fraud
excerpt: AI-driven deepfakes and synthetic IDs demand continuous fraud verification
content_html:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping the balance of power in security. Attackers are using AI to make deception look increasingly human while making fraud faster to execute, easier to scale and harder to detect. At the same time, security teams are turning to AI tools to identify and stop these threats.

Fraud is becoming more convincing, more sophisticated and more scalable, contributing to an estimated $9.5 trillion in global cybercrime damages each year. Attackers are bypassing traditional signals of legitimacy through deepfakes, synthetic identities and highly personalized phishing attempts.

There is no longer a single type of deepfake or attack variant. Each new generation of models improves on the last, and security controls must evolve to remain effective.

VP of Product Management at Mitek Systems.

Today, fraud has become more systematic. Rather than trying to break everything, attackers probe systems first, learn how defenses respond and focus on the weakest link.

Trust can no longer be established through a single verification point at the beginning of an interaction. Organizations need to evaluate trust continuously as behavior, context, and risk can change over a course of that interactions. The faster an organization can determine whether it is interacting with a legitimate user or a threat, the less opportunity for fraud to cause damage.

In this AI-driven environment, speed and accuracy in establishing trust are no longer differentiators. They are table stakes. The question facing security teams today is whether their identity verification infrastructure can adapt in real time to threats that are outpacing the models built to stop them.

How AI is making fraud feel legitimate

The same capabilities that allow AI to replicate human behavior and generate convincing content at scale are now being weaponized to make fraud feel indistinguishable from real activity. Attackers are using tools to bypass the signals security teams have traditionally depended on to separate legitimate users from threats.

What once requires insider-level knowledge of onboarding and identity workflows can now be generated on demand. Attackers have the visibility into how systems operate and where they are most vulnerable.

Identity-based attacks are evolving rapidly. Synthetic identities are increasingly passing initial identity verification checks, while voice clones can now be generated from just seconds of audio.

More advanced techniques like identity morphing are emerging. Attackers are combining their own facial features with a real people sourced online, creating hybrid identities that are harder to detect than traditional spoofing attempts.

At the same time, many attackers using advanced AI still miss foundational signals, including reused devices, repeated IP addresses or behavioral inconsistencies. That is why layered defenses still matter: newer attack methods do not eliminate the need for foundational controls.

This shift means that fraud is no longer presenting itself as an obvious intrusion. Instead, it blends into normal digital activity, making it harder to distinguish malicious behavior from legitimate engagement. Static trust signals and one-time verification steps are now increasingly insufficient on their own.

Why speed now determines outcomes

Since fraud is becoming embedded into everyday digital behavior, detection alone is no longer enough to keep pace. A critical factor is how quickly an organization can recognize risk and intervene before damage occurs.

Modern AI attacks are operating at machine speed and adapting tactics the moment they encounter resistance. Static checks and delayed reviews are struggling to keep pace, allowing fraud to move through workflows before defenses can respond.

However, as automation increases, attackers are also making more basic mistakes. They are caught reusing the same devices, IP addresses or behavioral patterns. As they focus on more advanced techniques, they are overlooking foundational signals. This is reinforcing that even simpler controls remain essential in a layered defense.

Fraud prevention must depend on real-time signals across the full interaction lifecycle. That means evaluating behavioral biometrics, device intelligence, identity signals and contextual risk together rather than in isolation.

Detecting subtle behavioral changes in real time allows organizations to challenge suspicious activity at the right moment, stopping AI-driven fraud before damage occurs rather than reacting after the threat has already succeeded. Keeping pace with AI-driven fraud means organizations must move beyond single checkpoints and implement layered defenses that validate trust across the whole journey.

Winning the AI vs. AI arms race requires layered, real-time defense

As AI lowers the barrier to fraud, security teams cannot rely on isolated controls or point-in-time checks. Attackers rapidly layer tactics, moving from one technique to the next as soon as initial trust is established, and static defenses are not adapting fast enough to keep pace.

Effective fraud prevention is not about replacing older controls with newer ones, but ensuring each layer evolves alongside new attack models.

The most effective defense strategy is not a single point of control. Identity, behavior, device intelligence and contextual signals need to be evaluated together and continually reassessed throughout the customer journey, not just at login.

Each layer has a role addressing a different fraud vector. Some are better suited to detecting advanced attacks, while others can catch basic mistakes. Both are equally necessary because attackers are often stopped at different points in the stack.

What it takes to win the trust race

Organizations should not have to choose between innovation and security to secure customers and operations. Building identity assurance so it can hold up as interactions become faster, more automated and easier to exploit requires treating verification as a continuous process rather than a one-time check.

AI has also lowered the barrier to entry for fraud. What once required insider knowledge or experience within financial systems can now be generated on demand, giving attackers visibility into how systems operate and how they can be bypassed.

Defending against AI-driven fraud requires evaluating identity, behavior, device signals and context together rather than in isolation. When controls are applied in isolation, gaps emerge. Fraud succeeds by exploiting those gaps between systems rather than defeating any single control.

The future of fraud prevention is continuous

Organizations still relying on static trust models will increasingly find themselves outpaced by AI-powered fraud that never slows down. What will separate effective security strategies is not the number of controls in place, but how effectively those controls work together.

Fraud is iterative and intelligence-driven, with attackers continuously refining their approach based on which defenses are easiest to bypass.

Every layer in a defense stack can catch what others miss, and fraud gets in by probing gaps between them. When a threat slips past the first layer, it will most likely be caught by the next layers. The more intelligently layered a security stack becomes, the greater the likelihood that suspicious activity will be identified and contained before damage occurs.

Continuous reassessment is what makes layered defense work in practice. Every interaction creates an opportunity to reassess trust based on evolving risk signals. A device linked to past fraud, behavioral patterns that do not match the established identity, or a login that appears legitimate but shows signs of automation are all indicators that risk has shifted.

This challenge is also expanding beyond identity. The same pressure is now emerging across payments, transactions and check-related fraud, widening the scope of what organizations need to defend.

If organizations want to keep pace, they must focus on closing gaps between layers and ensuring each control adapts as attack techniques evolve. AI is giving fraudsters the ability to probe systems, adapt in real time and make attacks increasingly difficult to distinguish from legitimate activity.

In this AI vs. AI environment, the only way to keep up is to stop treating verification as a single moment and start treating it as an ongoing discipline.

sentences.zh: 攻击者迅速分层战术，一旦建立了初始信任就从一种技术转向另一种技术，而静态防御的适应速度不够快，无法跟上步伐。

blocks.html_en: Effective fraud prevention is not about replacing older controls with newer ones, but ensuring each layer evolves alongside new attack models.

sentences.en: Effective fraud prevention is not about replacing older controls with newer ones, but ensuring each layer evolves alongside new attack models.
sentences.zh: 有效的欺诈预防并不是用新的控制措施取代旧的控制措施，而是确保每一层与新的攻击模型一起发展。

blocks.html_en: The most effective defense strategy is not a single point of control. Identity, behavior, device intelligence and contextual signals need to be evaluated together and continually reassessed throughout the customer journey, not just at login.

sentences.en: The most effective defense strategy is not a single point of control.
sentences.zh: 最有效的防御策略不是单点控制。

sentences.en: Identity, behavior, device intelligence and contextual signals need to be evaluated together and continually reassessed throughout the customer journey, not just at login.

blocks.html_en: Each layer has a role addressing a different fraud vector. Some are better suited to detecting advanced attacks, while others can catch basic mistakes. Both are equally necessary because attackers are often stopped at different points in the stack.

sentences.en: Each layer has a role addressing a different fraud vector.
sentences.zh: 每一层都有一个角色来应对不同的欺诈媒介。

sentences.en: Some are better suited to detecting advanced attacks, while others can catch basic mistakes.
sentences.zh: 有些更适合检测高级攻击，而另一些则可以发现基本错误。

sentences.en: Both are equally necessary because attackers are often stopped at different points in the stack.

blocks.html_en: Organizations should not have to choose between innovation and security to secure customers and operations. Building identity assurance so it can hold up as interactions become faster, more automated and easier to exploit requires treating verification as a continuous process rather than a one-time check.

sentences.en: Organizations should not have to choose between innovation and security to secure customers and operations.
sentences.zh: 组织不必在创新和安全之间做出选择，以确保客户和运营的安全。

sentences.en: Building identity assurance so it can hold up as interactions become faster, more automated and easier to exploit requires treating verification as a continuous process rather than a one-time check.
sentences.zh: 建立身份保证，使其能够随着交互变得更快、更自动化、更容易利用而持续存在，需要将验证视为一个持续的过程，而不是一次性检查。

blocks.html_en: AI has also lowered the barrier to entry for fraud. What once required insider knowledge or experience within financial systems can now be generated on demand, giving attackers visibility into how systems operate and how they can be bypassed.

sentences.en: AI has also lowered the barrier to entry for fraud.
sentences.zh: 人工智能还降低了欺诈的准入门槛。

sentences.en: What once required insider knowledge or experience within financial systems can now be generated on demand, giving attackers visibility into how systems operate and how they can be bypassed.
sentences.zh: 曾经需要金融系统内部知识或经验的内容现在可以按需生成，使攻击者能够了解系统如何运行以及如何绕过系统。

blocks.html_en: Defending against AI-driven fraud requires evaluating identity, behavior, device signals and context together rather than in isolation. When controls are applied in isolation, gaps emerge. Fraud succeeds by exploiting those gaps between systems rather than defeating any single control.

sentences.en: Defending against AI-driven fraud requires evaluating identity, behavior, device signals and context together rather than in isolation.
sentences.zh: 防御人工智能驱动的欺诈需要一起评估身份、行为、设备信号和上下文，而不是孤立地评估。

sentences.en: When controls are applied in isolation, gaps emerge.

sentences.en: Fraud succeeds by exploiting those gaps between systems rather than defeating any single control.

blocks.html_en: The future of fraud prevention is continuous

sentences.en: The future of fraud prevention is continuous
sentences.zh: 预防欺诈的未来是持续的

blocks.html_en: Organizations still relying on static trust models will increasingly find themselves outpaced by AI-powered fraud that never slows down. What will separate effective security strategies is not the number of controls in place, but how effectively those controls work together.

sentences.en: Organizations still relying on static trust models will increasingly find themselves outpaced by AI-powered fraud that never slows down.

sentences.en: What will separate effective security strategies is not the number of controls in place, but how effectively those controls work together.
sentences.zh: 区分有效安全策略的不是所采用的控制措施的数量，而是这些控制措施协同工作的有效性。

blocks.html_en: Fraud is iterative and intelligence-driven, with attackers continuously refining their approach based on which defenses are easiest to bypass.

sentences.en: Fraud is iterative and intelligence-driven, with attackers continuously refining their approach based on which defenses are easiest to bypass.
sentences.zh: 欺诈是迭代且由情报驱动的，攻击者根据最容易绕过的防御不断完善其方法。

blocks.html_en: Every layer in a defense stack can catch what others miss, and fraud gets in by probing gaps between them. When a threat slips past the first layer, it will most likely be caught by the next layers. The more intelligently layered a security stack becomes, the greater the likelihood that suspicious activity will be identified and contained before damage occurs.

sentences.en: Every layer in a defense stack can catch what others miss, and fraud gets in by probing gaps between them.
sentences.zh: 防御堆栈中的每一层都可以捕捉到其他层错过的信息，而欺诈行为则通过探测它们之间的差距而进入。

sentences.en: When a threat slips past the first layer, it will most likely be caught by the next layers.
sentences.zh: 当威胁溜过第一层时，它很可能会被下一层捕获。

sentences.en: The more intelligently layered a security stack becomes, the greater the likelihood that suspicious activity will be identified and contained before damage occurs.
sentences.zh: 安全堆栈的分层越智能，在损坏发生之前识别和遏制可疑活动的可能性就越大。

blocks.html_en: Continuous reassessment is what makes layered defense work in practice. Every interaction creates an opportunity to reassess trust based on evolving risk signals. A device linked to past fraud, behavioral patterns that do not match the established identity, or a login that appears legitimate but shows signs of automation are all indicators that risk has shifted.

sentences.en: Continuous reassessment is what makes layered defense work in practice.
sentences.zh: 持续的重新评估是分层防御在实践中发挥作用的原因。

sentences.en: Every interaction creates an opportunity to reassess trust based on evolving risk signals.
sentences.zh: 每次互动都会创造一个根据不断变化的风险信号重新评估信任的机会。

sentences.en: A device linked to past fraud, behavioral patterns that do not match the established identity, or a login that appears legitimate but shows signs of automation are all indicators that risk has shifted.
sentences.zh: 与过去的欺诈行为相关的设备、与既定身份不匹配的行为模式，或者看似合法但显示自动化迹象的登录，都是风险已经转移的指标。

blocks.html_en: This challenge is also expanding beyond identity. The same pressure is now emerging across payments, transactions and check-related fraud, widening the scope of what organizations need to defend.

sentences.en: This challenge is also expanding beyond identity.
sentences.zh: 这一挑战还扩展到身份之外。

sentences.en: The same pressure is now emerging across payments, transactions and check-related fraud, widening the scope of what organizations need to defend.
sentences.zh: 现在，支付、交易和支票相关欺诈领域也出现了同样的压力，扩大了组织需要防御的范围。

blocks.html_en: If organizations want to keep pace, they must focus on closing gaps between layers and ensuring each control adapts as attack techniques evolve. AI is giving fraudsters the ability to probe systems, adapt in real time and make attacks increasingly difficult to distinguish from legitimate activity.

sentences.en: If organizations want to keep pace, they must focus on closing gaps between layers and ensuring each control adapts as attack techniques evolve.
sentences.zh: 如果组织想要跟上步伐，他们必须专注于缩小各层之间的差距，并确保每个控制措施随着攻击技术的发展而适应。

sentences.en: AI is giving fraudsters the ability to probe systems, adapt in real time and make attacks increasingly difficult to distinguish from legitimate activity.
sentences.zh: 人工智能使欺诈者能够探测系统、实时适应并使攻击越来越难以与合法活动区分开来。

blocks.html_en: In this AI vs. AI environment, the only way to keep up is to stop treating verification as a single moment and start treating it as an ongoing discipline.

sentences.en: In this AI vs. AI environment, the only way to keep up is to stop treating verification as a single moment and start treating it as an ongoing discipline.

content_html_zh:
人工智能正在重塑安全领域的力量平衡。 攻击者正在利用人工智能让欺骗看起来越来越人性化，同时使欺诈执行得更快、更容易扩展、更难检测。 与此同时，安全团队正在转向人工智能工具来识别和阻止这些威胁。

欺诈正变得越来越令人信服、更加复杂且更具规模化，每年给全球网络犯罪造成的损失估计达 9.5 万亿美元。 攻击者通过深度伪造、合成身份和高度个性化的网络钓鱼尝试绕过传统的合法性信号。

不再存在单一类型的深度伪造或攻击变体。 每一代新一代模型都在上一代模型的基础上进行改进，安全控制必须不断发展才能保持有效。

Mitek Systems 产品管理副总裁。

如今，欺诈已变得更加系统化。 攻击者不会试图破坏一切，而是首先探测系统，了解防御措施如何响应，并专注于最薄弱的环节。

无法再在交互开始时通过单个验证点建立信任。 组织需要不断评估信任，因为行为、环境和风险可能会在交互过程中发生变化。 组织越快确定其正在与合法用户还是威胁进行交互，欺诈造成损害的机会就越少。

在这个人工智能驱动的环境中，建立信任的速度和准确性不再是区分因素。 它们是赌桌筹码。 如今安全团队面临的问题是，他们的身份验证基础设施是否能够实时适应威胁，这些威胁的速度超过了为阻止威胁而构建的模型。

人工智能如何让欺诈变得合法

人工智能能够复制人类行为并大规模生成令人信服的内容的相同功能现在被武器化，使欺诈感觉与真实活动难以区分。 攻击者正在使用工具绕过安全团队传统上用来区分合法用户和威胁的信号。

曾经需要内部人员级别的入职和身份工作流程知识的内容现在可以按需生成。 攻击者可以了解系统的运行方式以及最容易受到攻击的地方。

基于身份的攻击正在迅速发展。 合成身份越来越多地通过初始身份验证检查，而语音克隆现在只需几秒钟的音频即可生成。

身份变形等更先进的技术正在出现。 攻击者将自己的面部特征与在线获取的真实人物相结合，创建比传统欺骗尝试更难检测的混合身份。

与此同时，许多使用先进人工智能的攻击者仍然错过了基本信号，包括重复使用的设备、重复的 IP 地址或行为不一致。 这就是为什么分层防御仍然很重要：新的攻击方法并不能消除对基础控制的需求。

这种转变意味着欺诈不再表现为明显的入侵。 相反，它融入了正常的数字活动，使得区分恶意行为和合法行为变得更加困难。 现在，静态信任信号和一次性验证步骤本身已经越来越不够用了。

为什么现在速度决定结果

由于欺诈已融入日常数字行为中，仅靠检测已不足以跟上步伐。 一个关键因素是组织能够多快地识别风险并在损害发生之前进行干预。

现代人工智能攻击以机器速度运行，并在遇到阻力时调整策略。 静态检查和延迟审查正在努力跟上步伐，导致欺诈行为在防御措施做出响应之前就已经通过工作流程了。

然而，随着自动化程度的提高，攻击者也犯了更多基本错误。 他们被发现重复使用相同的设备、IP 地址或行为模式。 当他们专注于更先进的技术时，他们忽视了基础信号。 这进一步证明，在分层防御中，更简单的控制仍然至关重要。

欺诈预防必须依赖于整个交互生命周期中的实时信号。 这意味着要一起评估行为生物识别、设备智能、身份信号和情境风险，而不是单独评估。

实时检测细微的行为变化使组织能够在适当的时刻挑战可疑活动，在损害发生之前阻止人工智能驱动的欺诈，而不是在威胁成功后才做出反应。 与人工智能驱动的欺诈保持同步意味着组织必须超越单一检查点并实施分层防御以验证整个过程中的信任。

赢得人工智能与人工智能的军备竞赛需要分层的实时防御

随着人工智能降低欺诈门槛，安全团队不能依赖孤立的控制或时间点检查。 攻击者迅速分层战术，一旦建立了初始信任就从一种技术转向另一种技术，而静态防御的适应速度不够快，无法跟上步伐。

有效的欺诈预防并不是用新的控制措施取代旧的控制措施，而是确保每一层与新的攻击模型一起发展。

最有效的防御策略不是单点控制。 身份、行为、设备智能和上下文信号需要一起评估，并在整个客户旅程中不断重新评估，而不仅仅是在登录时。

每一层都有一个角色来应对不同的欺诈媒介。 有些更适合检测高级攻击，而另一些则可以发现基本错误。 两者同样必要，因为攻击者经常在堆栈中的不同点被阻止。

赢得信任竞赛需要什么

组织不必在创新和安全之间做出选择，以确保客户和运营的安全。 建立身份保证，使其能够随着交互变得更快、更自动化、更容易利用而持续存在，需要将验证视为一个持续的过程，而不是一次性检查。

人工智能还降低了欺诈的准入门槛。 曾经需要金融系统内部知识或经验的内容现在可以按需生成，使攻击者能够了解系统如何运行以及如何绕过系统。

防御人工智能驱动的欺诈需要一起评估身份、行为、设备信号和上下文，而不是孤立地评估。 当孤立地应用控制措施时，就会出现差距。 欺诈是通过利用系统之间的差距而不是破坏任何单一控制来成功的。

预防欺诈的未来是持续的

仍然依赖静态信任模型的组织将越来越多地发现自己被人工智能驱动的欺诈所超越，而且这种欺诈从未放缓。 区分有效安全策略的不是所采用的控制措施的数量，而是这些控制措施协同工作的有效性。

欺诈是迭代且由情报驱动的，攻击者根据最容易绕过的防御不断完善其方法。

防御堆栈中的每一层都可以捕捉到其他层错过的信息，而欺诈行为则通过探测它们之间的差距而进入。 当威胁溜过第一层时，它很可能会被下一层捕获。 安全堆栈的分层越智能，在损坏发生之前识别和遏制可疑活动的可能性就越大。

持续的重新评估是分层防御在实践中发挥作用的原因。 每次互动都会创造一个根据不断变化的风险信号重新评估信任的机会。 与过去的欺诈行为相关的设备、与既定身份不匹配的行为模式，或者看似合法但显示自动化迹象的登录，都是风险已经转移的指标。

这一挑战还扩展到身份之外。 现在，支付、交易和支票相关欺诈领域也出现了同样的压力，扩大了组织需要防御的范围。

如果组织想要跟上步伐，他们必须专注于缩小各层之间的差距，并确保每个控制措施随着攻击技术的发展而适应。 人工智能使欺诈者能够探测系统、实时适应并使攻击越来越难以与合法活动区分开来。

在这种人工智能与人工智能的环境中，跟上的唯一方法是停止将验证视为单一时刻，而开始将其视为一项持续的学科。
